public_comment.topic: Asked whether cost estimates for new hires fully factor in health insurance if the positions take benefits.

Asked how the salary-reserve-funded hires will appear in the FY27 budget comparison (as an increase or retroactively folded in), how the salary reserve itself is treated as a hiring mechanism over time, and questioned the ESSER-cuts discussion and the decision not to pursue the Chapter 70 warrant article immediately.

A resident (addressed afterward as Anna) argued the town has already given the schools substantial extra support through recent budget increases and free cash, and cautioned about sustainability of adding new positions against FY27's baseline budget growth.

Asked whether the $22,185 in Chapter 70 funds could be used for primary school supply needs, and expressed disappointment that purchased soccer uniforms were sitting undistributed while players use worn-out ones; noted fundraisers already run by teams.

budget_items.what_was_said: The business manager projected the combined salary cost of the new Turkey Hill paraprofessional and the IT hire against the salary reserve line, noting the para retiring this year largely offsets a new para's cost.
The business manager stated the full-year appropriated amount available in the salary reserve account as shown on the quarterly report.

The business manager said the health insurance line was running slightly under 25% spent through the first quarter, and that budgeting for new hires' benefits is based on current-year expenditure patterns.

budget_items.topic: Proposed out-of-district special ed/transportation reserve fund
budget_items.what_was_said: The proposed reserve fund under state law would be capped at a share of net school spending (based on actuals, not budgeted figures), to be funded automatically by any year-end school budget surplus.

budget_items.topic: Proposed comprehensive/forensic audit of FY25 books
budget_items.what_was_said: A committee member proposed using returned free cash to pay for an outside comprehensive audit of last year's books, with cost and scope still unknown; the idea was deferred pending further talks with the town manager.
The facilities director said the district's aging mower needs replacing and priced a comparable zero-turn model well below a brand-new equivalent.

Football and boys' soccer uniforms were purchased without a purchase order or superintendent approval and could not be returned once personalized; the committee discussed whether to adjust those teams' budgets to reflect the unsanctioned spending.

budget_items.topic: Town-side grant and cafeteria fund liabilities

budget_items.topic: History of recent district budget increases and free cash support
budget_items.what_was_said: A public commenter recounted recent fiscal-year budget percentage increases and the free cash contribution the town made toward the schools, arguing the community has already stepped up.

decisions.decision: Superintendent will likely request a DESE extension for the middle school exploration policy deadline, since there are not three school committee meetings before November 1.
Committee agreed, by withdrawing the motion, to seek the additional Chapter 70 money through the regular FY27 budget process instead of a November warrant article.
Decision on pursuing a comprehensive/forensic audit of FY25 books was deferred; the superintendent will talk with the town manager and bring back options and funding questions.
Generator removed from FY27 capital plan priority list and turf field added at priority four, with the rest of the ranking left unchanged after a tied vote on reordering the mower.
FY27 budget priorities discussion tabled until building principals' and the superintendent's budget priorities are available.

Undistributed soccer uniforms will be held and issued next year as the start of a new uniform replacement cycle; football's new uniforms count as its turn in that cycle, with no retroactive budget penalty to either team.
Committee signaled intent to develop a policy, via the policy subcommittee, requiring staff with spending authority to affirm they will not spend outside the certified budget without pre-approval.

minutes.headline: Committee backed a special-ed reserve-fund warrant article but withdrew a separate bid for extra Chapter 70 money
minutes.summary: The committee voted to put a special reserve fund for unbudgeted out-of-district special education and transportation costs on the November town meeting warrant, approved two new paraprofessional positions and restoring a full-time IT support position, and heard quarterly budget, athletics, and facilities reports. After extended debate, a second proposed warrant article to immediately appropriate roughly $22,185 in additional Chapter 70 funding was withdrawn in favor of seeking it through the regular FY27 budget process, and a proposal for an outside comprehensive/forensic audit of FY25 finances was deferred pending further talks with the town manager; the committee also discussed what to do about football and soccer uniforms that had been purchased without proper authorization.

what_happened.line: The committee voted to place a special reserve fund for unbudgeted out-of-district special education and transportation costs on the November town meeting warrant.
A separate warrant article seeking additional Chapter 70 funding, an amount as heard, was withdrawn in favor of pursuing it through the regular FY27 budget process.
The committee approved two new paraprofessional positions and restoring a full-time IT support position, both drawn from the salary reserve line.
A proposal for an outside comprehensive audit of FY25 finances, funded from returned free cash, was deferred pending talks with the town manager.
Football and soccer uniforms bought without required purchase-order approval will not be penalized retroactively; undistributed soccer uniforms will be held for next year's replacement rotation.

why_it_matters: The reserve fund is a warrant article residents will vote on at November town meeting; it would let year-end school budget surplus automatically cover special education placement and transportation costs that come in over budget.
Withdrawing the Chapter 70 warrant article means any additional state aid this year would not be spent immediately but would instead be weighed against other priorities in the FY27 budget process.

The unauthorized uniform purchases and the salary-reserve-funded hires prompted the committee to signal it will develop a policy requiring pre-approval before staff spend outside the certified budget.
